newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity ends higher, halts recent slide.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity ends higher, halts recent slide.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures finished higher Wednesday, halting a recent slide prompted by ample hydroelectric supplies, tepid heating demand and falling natural gas prices in the western U.S.
"It's been a long drop. It's a little bit of short-covering," said a West Coast futures trader.

The electricity complex was bolstered by news that the refueling outage of the 1,070 megawatt (MW) unit 2 at the San Onofre nuclear power plant could be extended by 10 to 15 days, some brokers and traders said.
The San Clemente, Calif., generating unit was shut November 30 for refueling and maintenance, and scheduled to begin startup February 8.

February California-Oregon Border (COB) futures settled up 41 cents at $13.64 a megawatt hour (MWh) after trading between $13.30 and $13.75. March COB ended up 16 cents at $11.65. February Palo Verde (PV) futures settled up 31 cents at $15.65/MWh after bouncing between $15.35 and $15.80. March PV finished up 20 cents at $13.80.
In the Northwest, Weather Services Corp said a strong area of low pressure is expected to effect the region bringing rain and snow and cooler temperatures for the weekend.

Down in the Southwest, showers and high-elevation snow will continue over parts of southern California, Nevada and northern Arizona through Thursday. Temperatures will average near to above normal through most of the week before arrival of a weekend cool front, the weather service said.

NYMEX February Henry Hub natgas futures settled down eight cents at $2.908 after a short-covering rally attempt fizzled. The spot gas contract reached as high as $3.000 late morning. February gas deliveries at the San Juan/Blanco Hub held near $2.55/mmBtu.
Market participants said today's uptick could continue Thursday, but the tenor of the market remained weak due to bearish fundamentals.
"You could see a sizable short-covering rally, but the overall tenor of the market hasn't changed," said another West Coast futures trader.
"It's definitely not a strong market. It'll probably trade sideways for awhile before it resumes its drop," echoed the first trader.
NYMEX estimated 334 COB and 216 PV contracts were sold. ((--New York Power Desk +1 212 859 1622))
